commitResults.messageBody:
Important assumptions in parsing, tasks, and storage are
implicit. A failed assumption currently surfaces as an
unrelated exception instead of a clear invariant failure.

Let's,
* add Java assert checks at those points
* enable assertions when running tests and the app

commitResults.messageTitle: Parser: Share task-index parsing for delete
commitResults.messageBody:
Mark, unmark, and delete all extract a 1-based task number from
the command line. Two near-identical helpers made the same logic
look like two different operations.

Let's parse all three commands through parseTaskIndex so a later
index-format change cannot drift between them.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Parser: Name deadline and event date prefixes
commitResults.messageBody:
Deadline and event parsing skipped past /by, /from, and /to using
raw offsets 3 and 5. Those numbers hide which delimiter they belong
to, so a prefix rename can silently cut the date in the wrong place.

Let's store the prefixes as named constants and use their lengths
when slicing the command.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Parser: Use guard clauses for task arguments
commitResults.messageBody:
Deadline validation nests the missing-date case inside a combined
empty check, and then trims strings that are already trimmed. That
hides the happy path and makes the reader re-check work already done.

Let's reject each missing field as soon as it is detected, keep the
successful parse un-indented, and store a trimmed todo description
the same way deadlines and events already do.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: TaskList: Filter matches with a stream
commitResults.messageBody:
find() walks the list with an index only to collect
descriptions that contain a keyword.

The index is unused beyond access, so a filter states the
intent more directly than a manual loop.

Let's replace the loop with a stream filter.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Storage: Load saved tasks with a stream
commitResults.messageBody:
load() skips blank and corrupted lines with continue
in a loop. That is a filter-map pipeline.

Let's use a stream so skipped lines are explicit stages
instead of control-flow jumps.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Storage: Map tasks to save lines with a stream
commitResults.messageBody:
save() builds a list of formatted lines with an index
loop. Each task maps to one line independently.

Let's replace the loop with a map so the
transformation is the whole story.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: TaskDateTime: Build formatters with a stream
commitResults.messageBody:
formatters() fills an array by index from pattern
strings. Each pattern maps to one formatter.

Let's map the patterns with a stream instead of
managing the array by hand.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Parser: Dispatch commands at one abstraction level
commitResults.messageBody:
parse() mixed command-word matching, substring offsets, and
argument errors in a long chain of near-duplicate branches. A
reader had to decode prefix slicing instead of following the
command table.

Let's match each command word once, hand the remaining text to a
helper, and keep parse() as a high-level dispatch list.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Alfred: Extract shared greeting and command handling
commitResults.messageBody:
The console loop and GUI entry points copy the same welcome, parse,
execute, save, and exit steps. That duplication mixes two levels of
abstraction and lets the two paths drift.

Let's keep run() and getResponse() as high-level flows and put the
shared steps in one place.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Event: Make inclusive date-range matching explicit
commitResults.messageBody:
occursOn() used a double-negative comparison against start and end
dates. Inclusive range checks are easy to misread when both bounds
are written as "not before" and "not after".

Let's name the two inclusive bounds so the condition matches the
method's documented meaning.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Ui: Share numbered task list formatting
commitResults.messageBody:
List, find, and on each built the same "n.displayText" line, with
the 1-based offset written inline. Copy-pasted numbering makes a
later display-format change easy to apply in only one of the three
places.

Let's format numbered tasks in one helper so the listing methods
stay at the level of choosing which tasks to show.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

Parameters named img, a local tmp list, and var db force the reader
to look up types and later assignments to learn what they hold.
The guidelines treat temp-style names as unexplained placeholders.

Let's use image, children, and dialogBox so each name states its
role.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Task: Name save-line fields and parse todos uniformly
commitResults.messageBody:
fromSaveLine() used raw lengths 3, 4, and 5 plus status bits "0"
and "1", and parsed todos inline while deadlines and events had
helpers. The numbers hide the save-file layout, and the mixed
shapes make similar cases look unrelated.

Let's name the field counts, indexes, and status markers, and parse
each task type through the same helper shape.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

parseSaved() nested a second try-catch inside the date-time failure
path. That arrowhead hides the real sequence: try an ISO date-time,
then fall back to a date-only value.

Let's parse each ISO form in its own helper so the fallback stays
un-nested.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Main: Name minimum chat window dimensions
commitResults.messageBody:
The stage minimum size was set with 220 and 417. Those values are
layout constraints, not obvious quantities, so a later resize looks
like an unexplained tweak.

Let's name the minimum height and width so the intent of the
constraint is visible at the call site.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: MainWindow: Name the goodbye close delay
commitResults.messageBody:
The GUI waits 1.5 seconds after bye before exiting so the farewell
can be read. A bare 1.5 hides that purpose and makes the pause look
like an arbitrary animation length.

Let's name the delay so the wait is obviously for the exit message.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Parser, Ui: Name the 1-based task numbering offset
commitResults.messageBody:
Users type and see task numbers starting at 1, while the list is
0-based. The conversion was a bare -1 or +1, which hides whether
the code is adjusting indexes or doing arithmetic on a count.

Let's name the offset so both parsing and display make the
user-facing numbering explicit.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Task: Parse save-file type icons through TaskType
commitResults.messageBody:
fromSaveLine() switched on the raw strings T, D, and E even though
those values already live on TaskType. Magic type letters and a
default-null branch hide that the save format only allows the
known task kinds.

Let's resolve the icon to the enum and switch on TaskType so a new
kind becomes a compiler-checked case instead of another string.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: TaskList: Name the find keyword and iterate tasks directly
commitResults.messageBody:
find() called the lowercase keyword needle and walked the list by
index even though the index was never shown. needle is jargon, and
get(i) twice makes a simple membership check look like positional
work.

Let's call it what it is, a normalized keyword, and iterate the
tasks themselves.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Storage: Write save lines without an unused index
commitResults.messageBody:
save() walked the task list by index only to call toSaveFormat() on
each element. An unused index suggests the position matters when
the file format is just one line per task in order.

Let's iterate the tasks directly so the write loop matches that
story.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
Add Java assertions for core invariants

Master added Java asserts on the pre-refactor Parser, Storage, and
Alfred shapes. Taking those versions wholesale would restore the
old index loops and parseDeleteIndex signature.

Let's keep CodeQuality's helpers and loops, and re-apply the
asserts onto those methods so both sets of work stay intact.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
Branch a code quality

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge CodeQuality and assertions into Streams
commitResults.messageBody:
Master brought refactors and asserts that still used for-loops in
Storage.save() and TaskList.find(). Taking those versions would
drop this branch's stream pipelines.

Let's keep the streams, use the CodeQuality names, and check the
same invariants inside those pipelines.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
Branch a streams

The README explains how to run Alfred but not which commands it
accepts.

Users following the setup steps have no accurate reference for
command syntax, date formats, or task numbering.

Let's add a Using CLI commands section that matches Parser and
the command classes.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

Task save lines have no marker for archived tasks.

Archive must survive a restart without treating an old
description of A as the archive flag.

Let's,
* append A or UA as an extra field on every save line
* load the flag by field count so legacy lines stay live

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: TaskList: Split live and archive views
commitResults.messageBody:
The task list treats every stored task as live.

Archive needs live numbering, archive numbering, and a rollback
snapshot when a save fails.

Let's,
* map live and archive indexes onto one backing list
* restore archived tasks to the end of the live list

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

Users cannot hide old tasks from the live list without deleting them.

Archive, restore, and delete archive belong next to the existing
list and delete commands, with the same replies in GUI and console.

Let's,
* parse archive, restore, list archive, and delete archive
* persist every stored task and roll back memory if saving fails

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

The User Guide does not mention archive commands.

Users need the command list and a UI script to check the new
behavior.

Let's,
* document archive, restore, and delete archive
* add UI test-plan cases for those commands

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: GUI: Distinguish error and list replies
commitResults.messageBody:
Alfred replies all share one bubble style, so the GUI cannot
tell errors and lists from ordinary conversation.

Let's record NORMAL, ERROR, and LIST on each Ui reply, expose
the latest style from Alfred, and apply matching CSS classes
on Alfred dialog boxes.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Pad list numbers to two digits
commitResults.messageBody:
List numbers 1. and 10. shift the type column even when the
GUI uses a monospace font.

Let's pad live, archive, find, and on lists to width 2 so
single-digit numbers stay aligned.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: GUI: Tighten layout and window chrome
commitResults.messageBody:
99px avatars crowd the 400px window, so list lines wrap. The
command field also sits flush to the edge and starts unfocused.

Let's shrink avatars, reduce bubble padding, pad the text field,
set the window icon, and focus the command field on launch.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Add help command with a compact syntax list
commitResults.messageBody:
Users have no in-app list of commands, so they must remember
syntax or open the user guide.

Let's add a help command that prints one syntax line per
command and rejects extra arguments.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

An unknown command only says the request is not recognised, so
users have no next step.

Let's tell them to type help, using the existing error bubble.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

The user guide does not mention help, so users would only
discover it after an unrecognized command.

Let's document help syntax and that unknown input points to it.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
